subject: Including observer as covariate in detection model for species occupancy model

messages.author: 0141b24755b40cf8
messages.subject: Including observer as covariate in detection model for species occupancy model
parts:
Hi all,

I am inexperienced in working with double observer detection modeling and just want to clarify a few things, and this seems like the best place to post.

I have a double observer data set where sites were visited one time in a season. This results in a dataset with the following columns:

Species ob1 ob2 ob1ID ob2ID
AMCR    1     1        Jane    John
 . . . .

I was assuming that one could use the observer ID (ob1ID or ob2ID) directly in the observation process, but most of the examples I have seen in unmarked (eg. gmultmix example) have more than 2 observations at a site. Am I correct in assuming that with only one site visit, it is going to be difficult to explicitly include observer ID? If one can use observer ID directly in, say, the occ() model, how does one format the data?

Any advice would be appreciated,

Wade

messages.author: 20119867e986c754
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Including observer as covariate in detection model for species occupancy model
parts:
With this setup of the data, it seems to me that observer is analogous to sample occasion (you have two "samples", but instead of being different in time, they are different in observer). So, it looks like you could just model it like you would sample-specific detection probability to see if there are differences between observers.
Here's how I would do it:

# First simulate some data
n = 100 # number of sites
S = 2 # number of samples
D = matrix(0,n,S) # the detection matrix
p1 = .7 # detection prob for Jane
p2 = .5 # detection prob for John
D[,1] <- rbinom(n,1,p1)
D[,2] <- rbinom(n,1,p2)
Obs1 <- rep("Jane",100)
Obs2 <- rep("John",100)
sim.Data <- data.frame(D,Obs1,Obs2)

# Here's the sample dataset similar to what you showed:
head(sim.Data)

# Now get it into unmarked:
y <- sim.Data[1:2]
Observer <- sim.Data[,3:4]
sim.UMF <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y=y, obsCovs = list(Observer=Observer))
summary(sim.UMF)

#Now you can see if AIC model selection finds an observer effect:
m0 <- occu(~1~1, data=sim.UMF)
m1 <- occu(~Observer~1, data=sim.UMF)

models <- fitList('p(.)psi(.)' = m0,
                  'p(Obs)psi(.)' = m1)
ms <- modSel(models)
ms

# And it does.

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Including observer as covariate in detection model for species occupancy model
parts:
Thanks for the example. That makes sense. Unfortunately, the dataset that I have has more than one group of double observers, so the data actually looks more like this:

Species site ob1 ob2 ob1ID ob2ID
AMCR    A     1     1        Jane    John
 . . . .
AMCR   B       1    0          Fred    Barbara

The ob1 and ob2 then are mixtures of individuals. For the most part, sites were only visited once, so the ob1 and ob2 columns (with observed/ not observed data) currently represent a mixture of observers.

I guess there are two ways that I can go. First, I could separate species by observers and get individual estimates for observers and do kind of an ad hoc viewing of the detection probability estimates. Second,  I was thinking that I could simply randomize the ob1 and ob2 by rows. I am not sure if anyone does what I am suggesting here, and just wanting to see what people thought.

I know that ideally I would have a dataset with multiple site visits through a season per observer-group, but they weren't able to do that for a variety of reasons.

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Including observer as covariate in detection model for species occupancy model
parts:
Hi Wade-

I think you're making this harder than it needs to be. I gave you the example of two observer names, but you could use more without changing the code at all. Unmarked is seeing the names as factors and handles them appropriately in the analysis. To convince you, I changed my code to make up the simulated data to have 4 observers, each with a different p. Note that I always had 2 names in the first column, and the 2 other names in the second column, but I only did that so that it wouldn't pick the same name twice in one sample. In your real example any observer name could be in the first or second column.

If you run it, you see that unmarked makes Barbara the intercept because it goes alphabetical. Looking at the results of m1 you see that it found Barbara had the highest p, followed by Jane, John, and Fred, respectively. That matches the true values used for simulation nicely.

Try it:

# First simulate some data
n = 100 # number of sites
S = 2 # number of samples
D = matrix(0,n,S) # the detection matrix

Obsa <- c("Jane", "John") #choose random observers for obs1
Obsb <- c("Barbara", "Fred") #choose random observers for obs2
Obs1 <- sample(Obsa,n, replace=TRUE)
Obs2 <- sample(Obsb,n, replace=TRUE)

pJane = 0.7
pJohn = 0.5
pBarb = 0.8
pFred = 0.4

p1 <- vector(length=length(Obs1))
for(i in 1:length(Obs1)){
  ifelse(Obs1[i]=="Jane", p1[i] <- pJane, p1[i] <- pJohn)
}

p2 <- vector(length=length(Obs2))
for(i in 1:length(Obs2)){
  ifelse(Obs2[i]=="Barbara", p2[i] <- pBarb, p2[i] <- pFred)

sim.Data <- data.frame(D,Obs1,Obs2)

# Here's the sample dataset similar to what you showed:
head(sim.Data)

# Now get it into unmarked:
y <- sim.Data[1:2]
Observer <- sim.Data[,3:4]
sim.UMF <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y=y, obsCovs = list(Observer=Observer))
summary(sim.UMF)

#Now you can see if AIC model selection finds an observer effect:
m0 <- occu(~1~1, data=sim.UMF)
m1 <- occu(~Observer~1, data=sim.UMF)

models <- fitList('p(.)psi(.)' = m0,
                  'p(Obs)psi(.)' = m1)
ms <- modSel(models)
ms

# And it does.
